_about: Record-level overrides for concept ids that mix two meanings (curated 2026-10-15, user-approved; see PHASE2.md). Each split maps one (digest, normalised id) record to a disambiguated id, chosen by reading that record's definition. Applied by scripts/build_kg.py after id normalisation and before aliases.json; the digests are not edited. 'spine' re-points a canon spine id whose plain name is now split to the sense its canon definition has. The plain id gets a generated disambiguation page.

splits.why: 'S-shaped curve over gains and losses from a reference point': prospect theory's value function
'v*(t,x), the optimal cost-to-go; it determines pi*': dynamic-programming / RL value function
'framing primes values differentially, establishing salience': media priming
'media ... are far more successful at changing what we think about': media effect (agenda-setting/priming)
'an idea or number automatically activates compatible thoughts': cognitive (associative) priming
'the majority-decision paradox explored by Condorcet and Dodgson': Condorcet cycle (same sense as Arrow ch01's existing paradox-of-voting-cycle)
'majority decision violates Condition 1 for more than two alternatives': Condorcet cycle
'since a decisive vote is very unlikely, information for voting is not worth buying': Downs's decisive-vote paradox
'voting is costly and one vote is very unlikely to decide': turnout paradox
'the chance of making or breaking a tie is tiny, so instrumental voting seems irrational': turnout paradox
'group statement accepted ... as fact about every member': social-cognition stereotype (Lippmann's sense stays stereotype-lippmann)
'the conventional (possibly inaccurate) idea of a kind that speakers must acquire': Putnam's semantic stereotype

senses.value-function-econ: prospect theory: S-shaped value of gains and losses from a reference point
senses.value-function-rl: dynamic programming / RL / optimal control: optimal cost-to-go or expected return
senses.priming-media: media priming: emphasis changes the standards used to judge leaders or issues
senses.priming-cognitive: cognitive priming: an idea automatically activates related ideas
senses.paradox-of-voting-cycle: Condorcet: pairwise majority preferences can cycle
senses.paradox-of-voting-turnout: Downs: one vote is almost never decisive, so costly voting seems irrational
senses.stereotype-social: social cognition: a belief about a group applied to its members
senses.stereotype-semantic: Putnam: the conventional idea of a kind that a speaker must acquire
senses.stereotype-lippmann: Lippmann: a culturally supplied picture in the head that shapes perception
